question: As per the NITI Aayog's multi-dimensional Poverty Index, which of the following state has highest percentage population classified as poor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Multidimensional Poverty Index** was released by **NITI Aayog.**
 
• The MPI strives to** quantify poverty **across its various facets.
 
• It supplements** current statistics on poverty **based on **per capita consumer expenditure.**
 
• It has three equally weighted dimensions:** standard of living, health, and education.**
 
• **Twelve variables**, including **food intake, school attendance, years of schooling, drinking water, sanitation, housing, and bank accounts**, are used to reflect these three aspects.
 
• This **baseline report **of the national MPI measure is based on the **reference period of 2015-16 of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-4).**
 
• The majority of the population of the state is** multidimensionally poorest** in** Bihar,** followed by** Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• The state with the **lowest rates of poverty** was** Kerala**, which was followed by **Puducherry, Lakshadweep, Goa, and Sikkim.**
 
• The states of **Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh** have the **most malnourished citizens.**
 
• MPI is a contribution towards measuring progress towards target** 1.2 of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• Target aims at reducing “**at least by half** the proportion of men, women and children of all ages** living in poverty** in all its dimensions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Oxford Poverty & Human Development Initiative** and the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** together released the** Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021.**
 
• **5.9 billion** people's data from **109 nations** are taken into account by the Index.
 
• In terms of the **Global MPI 2021,** India is ranked** 66th out of 109 nations.**
